Links: [{"title":"EU legislators agree to delay for high-risk AI rules","url":"https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/eu-legislators-agree-to-delay-for-high-5617765/"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www.onetrust.com/pt/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"},{"title":"EU Delays ‘High Risk’ AI Rules to 2027 After Tech Pushback","url":"https://www.tovima.com/world/eu-delays-high-risk-ai-rules-to-2027-after-tech-pushback/amp"},{"title":"kiosk.youboox.fr","url":"https://kiosk.youboox.fr/en/pod/588/rss/103/article/310345837"},{"title":"eu commission proposes delay to ai act to 2027 amid digital omnibus proposal","url":"https://www.bhrrc.org/es/latest-news/eu-commission-proposes-delay-to-ai-act-to-2027-amid-digital-omnibus-proposal/"},{"title":"eu commission proposes delay to ai act to 2027 amid digital omnibus proposal","url":"https://www.bhrrc.org/ko/최신-뉴스/eu-commission-proposes-delay-to-ai-act-to-2027-amid-digital-omnibus-proposal/"},{"title":"EU’s Digital Omnibus proposes major delay to AI Act high-risk rules","url":"https://cadeproject.org/updates/eus-digital-omnibus-proposes-major-delay-to-ai-act-high-risk-rules/"},{"title":"EU’s Digital Omnibus proposes major delay to AI Act high-risk rules","url":"https://cadeproject.org/?p=152564"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www-onetrust-com.ezproxy.tees.ac.uk/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"},{"title":"eu digital omnibus proposes delay of ai compliance deadlines","url":"https://www-onetrust-com.ezproxy.nottingham.edu.cn/blog/eu-digital-omnibus-proposes-delay-of-ai-compliance-deadlines/"}]

The most recent item I found is a provisional deal, not a this-week development. The search didn't surface any news from the past few days, so I can't confirm whether the formal adoption has happened since.

- **Provisional agreement (May 2026):** On May 7, 2026, the Council of the EU and the European Parliament announced their provisional agreement on targeted amendments to the EU AI Act, as part of the Digital Omnibus. The delay is intended to provide businesses with additional time to achieve compliance.
- **Original proposal (November 2025):** The Commission proposed moving Annex III high-risk obligations no longer take effect in August 2026 as originally planned. Instead, companies would have until the end of 2027 to comply. Annex I product-linked systems would shift even further, to August 2028.
- **Rationale:** Commentators cited missing harmonized technical standards and many EU member states still lack operational supervisory authorities as reasons the 2026 deadlines weren't workable.
- **Other changes:** The package also pushes machine-readable detection of AI-generated content to February 2027 for systems already on the market.

For the latest status, I'd check the Council or Parliament press releases directly, since my results don't show whether the agreement has been formally adopted or published in the Official Journal.

The main news is that the EU AI Office has started enforcing the AI Act, though these reports are recent and not all from major outlets.

- **First enforcement steps:** Speaking in Dublin on 14 October, Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office has sent information requests covering security, external evaluation, and model-use monitoring. "Our AI Office has started enforcing these rules, and sent requests for information addressing issues such as security, external evaluation and monitoring how models are used," Euronews reports these requests went to OpenAI and Anthropic over two summer incidents. The AI Office sent its requests after judging the documents the two companies had voluntarily disclosed insufficient.
- **Fines procedure:** A draft Commission implementing regulation, dated 12 October, sets out how the AI Office would run proceedings that could lead to fines, covering file access, trade secrets, and limitation periods. The draft on Articles 75c and 75d of the AI Act stays open for consultation until November 9, 2026. One outlet says the Commission expects adoption by the end of 2026.
- **Timeline:** Article 50 transparency rules have applied since 2 August 2026, according to ActuIA. The next deadline is 2 December 2026, when new prohibitions and output-marking duties take effect. High-risk obligations were pushed back to 2 December 2027 by the omnibus simplification package, per the same source.
- **Dublin Declaration:** Ireland presented the Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI at the same summit, focused on cooperation, security, and infrastructure rather than new legal obligations, according to Tech Insider.
- **Caveat:** The lab-incident probes rest on press reports, and I did not find the Commission's own primary notice of formal probes. The GDPR-side "data omnibus" is still unsettled, with no Council mandate as of early October, per Swfte.

content.text:
Here is what turned up for roughly 9–16 October 2026. Most of it comes from secondary outlets. I found no primary Commission notice.

**Enforcement**
- Henna Virkkunen, the Commission's executive vice-president for tech, said in Dublin on 14 October that the AI Office "has started enforcing these rules." It has sent information requests on security, external evaluation and monitoring of model use.
- Euronews reports the requests went to OpenAI and Anthropic over two summer incidents. The AI Office reportedly judged their voluntary disclosures insufficient.
- Caveat: the reports about probes into OpenAI and Anthropic rest on press coverage, and I found no confirmation from the Commission itself.

**Fining procedure**
- A draft Commission implementing regulation, dated 12 October, sets out how AI Office proceedings that could lead to fines would run. It covers file access, trade secrets and limitation periods.
- It is open for consultation until 9 November 2026. One outlet says the Commission expects to adopt it by the end of 2026.

**Timeline**
- Article 50 transparency rules have applied since 2 August 2026.
- The next deadline is 2 December 2026, when new prohibitions and output-marking duties take effect.
- The Digital Omnibus moves high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027, according to ActuIA.
- The Council and Parliament reached a provisional agreement on the omnibus on 7 May 2026. I couldn't confirm from these results whether it has been formally published.

**Other**
- Ireland presented the Dublin Declaration on Reliable, Secure and Sovereign AI at the same summit. It focuses on cooperation, security and infrastructure rather than new legal obligations.
